proposal.name: Draft and ratify a PRD's plan of issues

plan.name: Draft and ratify a PRD's plan of issues
plan.summary: This is the first half of #112, drafting a plan: a writer's `/invariant plan` on an issue that holds or links a PRD has the factory draft a plan of issues, post it with its hash, and record a writer's `/invariant ratify` of it. In internal/formalize, an IssuePlan is a name, a summary and 1 to MaxIssues (10) issues in order, each a title and a complete body with either a Project: line naming a clean directory in the repository (modeled) or a Kind: plumbing line and no Code: line (plumbing), never both, and no /invariant command line; its sha256 hash covers the name, the summary and every title and body, in order. Request.PRD, the base branch exported, makes Formalize run a planning agent on request.md and the repository in repo/, with a check tool that `invariant mcp -issues` serves, then read the agent's issues.json back as Proposal.IssuePlan, pinned by its hash, or proposal.json's forks or unsupported as a plumbing draft is read, and a plan that breaks the rules comes back as the result's problem. Once a writer asks, the factory treats the issue as a PRD through its forks, answers and revisions, whatever its own Kind:, Project: or Code: lines say; its proposal post shows the plan's name and each issue's title and whole body, in order, with the ratify command; and a writer's ratify, checked against the issue protocol as any proposal's is, gets one ratified post that answers the ratifying comment and names the ratifier and the hash, with no branch, build or pull request. Left for later issues: working a ratified plan against factory/plans (opening its issues one at a time, in order, each once the one before has merged, recording each on the plan's issue, saying when it's done, and stopping at /invariant stop), and taking each opened issue on the ratifier's authority.

tests.name: TestAPRDIsDraftedAsAPlanOfIssues
tests.says: With a PRD, the planning agent gets the request, the repository and a check tool, and the issues.json it leaves comes back as a plan of issues pinned by its hash.

tests.name: TestAPRDsDraftAsksOrFailsAsADraftDoes
tests.says: A PRD's draft can ask forks in proposal.json instead, and a plan that breaks the rules comes back as a problem, with nothing to ratify.

tests.name: TestAPlanOfIssuesMustHoldTogether
tests.says: A plan needs a name, a summary and 1 to 10 issues, each with a title and a body that is modeled (a clean Project: line) or plumbing (Kind: plumbing, no Code: line), never both, and carries no /invariant command.

tests.name: TestAPlanOfIssuesHashesWhatIsRatified
tests.says: The plan's hash changes with its name, its summary, any issue's title or body, and the issues' order.

tests.name: TestAPlanCommandProposesAPlanOfIssues
tests.says: A writer's /invariant plan, and no one else's, drafts a plan of issues against the base branch whatever the issue's own Kind: line says, and posts its name and each issue's title and body, in order, with the ratify command.

tests.name: TestAPlanOfIssuesAsksItsForksAndRevises
tests.says: The PRD's forks come first, and answering them or asking for a revision drafts a plan of issues again, the revision starting from the plan before it.

tests.name: TestRatifyingAPlanOfIssuesRecordsItAndBuildsNothing
tests.says: Ratifying the plan posts once that it's ratified, answering the ratifying comment and naming the ratifier and the hash, and the issue stops awaiting ratification, with nothing built, pushed or opened as a pull request.

usage.summary: I planned the first half of #112, drafting a plan: a writer's `/invariant plan` makes a new planning agent write a checked, hash-pinned plan of 1 to 10 issues, the factory posts it for ratification, and `/invariant ratify` records it without building anything. Working the ratified plan against `factory/plans` (including `/invariant stop`) and taking each opened issue on the ratifier's authority are left for later issues; the check passed on the first try with all 7 acceptance tests failing on the current code, and since the change touches the trusted base, a person merges it.
